In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new data model for spatial data types in database systems, and the development of a prototype implementation of the new model in the Postgres object-relational DBMS.
the development of a new database concept called realms, and with the use of realms as a foundation for spatial data types in database systems.
the development and implementation of a general, consistent, robust, and efficient spatial data model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a spatial data type in a DBMS can be viewed as a pair (D, R), where D is a domain and R is a realm, and where the realm is the geometric domain underlying the domain.
the realm layer offers an elegant and efficient solution to the problem of spatial data types in database systems.
realms are a foundation for spatial data types in database systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a spatial algebra over a geometric realm is a fully general and fully consistent spatial algebra.

the realm approach is an alternative to object-relational systems in the sense that it is a way to add spatial types to a relational DBMS without changing the relational data model, but with the advantage of a more general and more powerful data model.

we have defined a spatial data type that is (i) fully general and closed under set operations; (ii) has a formal semantics; (iii) uses finite representations; (iv) offers facilities for enforcing geometric consistency; and (v) cooperates with any DBMS data model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a geometric domain is a good abstraction for spatial data types in DBMS.
a spatial data type is a data type over a realm.
realms provide a new, powerful, and elegant way to implement spatial data types and algebras in database systems.
